terra.problem: The text says they bow down, not that they get on their knees or that their walk ends there.
The negotiation and price-tag jokes make light of people coming over in chains.
Comparing people coming over in chains to someone following the smell of cookies makes light of their situation.
The jokes about sneaking out and a quiet parade make the disgraced idol makers the target of the humor.
The explanation attributes the statement about shame and humiliation to the LORD as a direct speaker, but verse 16 is narration.
The verse does not say that nobody carries anything when the idol makers depart.
Verse 17 is narration, but the explanation attributes its words directly to the LORD.
Verse 17 is narration, not a direct statement by the LORD. The conclusion that Israel has no running to do also goes beyond what the verse says.
Verse 17 is narration, but the explanation says the LORD speaks its statements directly.
The explanation attributes the narrator's statement about why the earth was formed directly to the LORD.
The explanation attributes the narrator's statement about why the earth was formed directly to the LORD.
The explanation says needing to carry the god is the problem. The verse says the god cannot save, but does not give that as the reason.
The idol makers depart in disgrace in verse 16, not in the preceding verse, verse 20.

The explanation identifies everyone whose knee bows and tongue swears allegiance as those who say righteousness and strength are in the LORD alone. The passage does not explicitly identify the speakers that way.
The passage says Israel's descendants will exult, but it does not say that nobody is mourning.
Verses 17 and 25 are narration, but the explanation attributes their statements directly to the LORD. Verse 17 is not immediately before verse 25, and neither verse says nobody is lost.
